higher_level_requirement: The DPU-BOOT CSC shall create a record of failed DRAM blocks, BIT_DRAM, in the SYSTEM_BLOCK.

The Stage 2 BIT includes a test of the SCM EDAC circuit, a checksum test on SCM PROM, a MIL-STD-1553B internal BIT, and a memory test of the DCI Data Buffers. The results of the BIT are recorded in the SYS_CNFG_AREA in EEPROM and are also maintained in DRAM. If an error occurs in one of the functions performing the BIT, the test result will be reported as a failure in the test itself.

rationale: The lower-level requirement describes the Built-In Test component performing Stage 2 memory-related tests and recording BIT results in persistent system configuration storage and DRAM. rationale: The lower-level requirement refines the Bootstrap program’s interaction with DRAM by specifying that Stage 1 Built-In Test, which is included in the Bootstrap program, contains a DRAM BIT. The lower-level requirement does not address VME or IOCC, but it provides a concrete Bootstrap function contributing to the DRAM portion of the higher-level requirement.

higher_level_requirement: At the end of a download, the Bootstrap Monitor of the DPU-BOOT CSC shall compute a CHKS_32 on the X stored in EEPROM and compare it against the CHKS_32 sent with the X during the transfer. The Bootstrap Monitor shall output to to the RS-232 interface both CHKS_32s and a message indicating whether the download was successful.

By defining a library function that computes a checksum over a specified memory range using XOR, it operationalizes the mechanism for calculating the CHKS_32 over the EEPROM-stored data so it can be compared with the transferred checksum. Although it does not cover the RS-232 output or success message behavior, it directly supports the checksum computation portion of the higher-level requirement.

higher_level_requirement: The Bootstrap CSC shall address hardware modules as defined in document 1400, Company X Specification for the Company X Communication/Memory Module.
lower_level_requirement: DRAM BITPart of the memory is tested in Boot Sequence 1, and part of the memory is tested during Boot Sequence 2. During Boot Sequence 1, ? KB of DRAM is tested before the Bootstrap is copied to this area. During Boot Sequence 2, the remaining memory is tested in ? KB blocks. The DRAM BIT first writes the address of each word in a block to that word in the block. Then the test flushes the cache and reads back the entire block. If a single-bit error occurs on the read-back, the location is read again. If another single-bit error occurs, the test assumes a hard error and marks the whole block bad. If a multiple-bit error occurs, the whole block is marked bad. If the value read back does not match the address, the whole block is marked bad. This same process is repeated with the ones complement of the address. The Bootstrap stores the results of the DRAM BIT in EEPROM as a series of x consecutive y-bit words. Each bit in a result word represents the result of testing a ? KB block of DRAM. These bits are mapped to DRAM by proceeding from least-significant bit (LSb) to most-significant bit (MSb) as the addresses of the memory blocks increase. A set bit indicates that a block of DRAM has failed. A clear bit indicates that a block of DRAM has passed the test.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement directly operationalizes how the Bootstrap CSC addresses a hardware memory module, specifically DRAM, by defining its built-in test behavior, block mapping, error handling, and result storage. Since the higher-level requirement requires the Bootstrap CSC to address hardware modules defined by the communication/memory module specification, detailed DRAM testing and representation of memory block status is a concrete implementation for that memory hardware module.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-BOOT CSC shall perform successive writes to a word page of EEPROM within C msecs, or wait a minimum of D usecs between successive writes.
lower_level_requirement: Hardware InterfacesThe DPU-BOOTSTRAP must interface directly with the EEPROM on the Company X Communication Module. The DPU-BOOTSTRAP accesses EEPROM as ?-bit words only. The specific timing requirements of the EEPROM are satisfied in one of three ways:* the timing requirements are met by inserting specific wait loops (typical),* the timing requirements are met by use of the EEPROM Driver (DOWNLOAD command), andthe timing requirements are met implicitly by the amount of time which will be required to execute the intervening instructions regardless of the CPU speed setting (DRAM test logic).
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement directly refines how DPU-BOOTSTRAP satisfies EEPROM access timing constraints, including inserting wait loops, using an EEPROM driver, or relying on intervening instruction time. This operationalizes the higher-level requirement’s constraint on timing between successive EEPROM word writes by specifying implementation mechanisms that ensure the EEPROM timing requirements are met.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-CCM shall strobe the Watchdog timer by writing to the SCM_WDR at an interval of 1 second.
lower_level_requirement: Startup Sequence On flight, a power cycle can only be effected by the SCU. A watchdog reset could be induced by the DPU FSW due to a detected, unrecoverable error, or it could occur as a by-product of the FSW entering a state in which it fails to strobe the watchdog timer. On boot, the bootstrap tests and clears DRAM, and then proceeds to load the DPU FSW from EEPROM and executes it. The DPU FSW then loads configuration information from EEPROM (which establishes various operational defaults) and spawns the various DPU FSW tasks.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement directly references the DPU flight software failing to strobe the watchdog timer as a condition that can lead to a watchdog reset. This operational context depends on the higher-level behavior that the DPU-CCM normally strobes the watchdog by writing to SCM_WDR at a fixed interval. Therefore, the lower-level startup/reset behavior refines the consequence and system role of the required watchdog strobing behavior.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-CCM shall provide a command to reboot the DPU.
lower_level_requirement: Watchdog LibraryThe DPU contains a hardware watchdog which must be strobed periodically in order to prevent a DPU reboot.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement identifies the hardware mechanism that causes a DPU reboot when the watchdog is not periodically strobed. higher_level_requirement: The DPU-CCM shall forward ACS_MSGs to the DPU-DPA for processing immediately upon receipt (I.e. shall not enqueue the message to the command dispatcher queue).
lower_level_requirement: Error Collection and ReportingThe DPU-CCM CSC provides a centralized error reporting interface, ccmErrEnq(), that other FSW tasks use to report errors. Each time it wakes, ccmTask() checks to see if it is time to form an error/event packet for transmission to the ground. If so, ccmTask() calls ccmHkMkError() to actually create the packet and forward it to DPU-SCUI for transmission to the ground.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement specifies a DPU-CCM behavior in which ccmTask() creates an error/event packet and forwards it to another DPU component, DPU-SCUI, for downstream transmission. This operationalizes the higher-level requirement’s concern that DPU-CCM must forward relevant messages onward for processing/transmission rather than retain them locally, by describing a concrete forwarding path for generated packets. The relationship is direct because both requirements constrain DPU-CCM message-handling behavior and require forwarding out of the DPU-CCM component.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-CCM shall quietly discard any unrecognized observatory messages (I.e. messages which do not have a DPU command APID).
lower_level_requirement: Memory Upload and Download HandlingIf more than 65535 bytes need to be uploaded, the upload file must be broken up into multiple smaller files, each less than or equal to 65535 bytes, and then each of the virtual uploads should be sent in series. Because of the sequence numbers, the DPU FSW can receive individual upload commands out of sequence. There is no time limit for the accomplishment of a single virtual upload, and so a long upload can continue across ground contacts. If an upload is in progress, the last sequence number can be sent to the DPU FSW and it will report the list of missing sequence numbers via event number S_ccm_MISSING_SEQNO. If an upload is in progress and needs to be cancelled, it can be discarded by issuing the D_MEM_DAT_CNCL command.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement specifies operational behavior for DPU-CCM memory upload/download command handling, including how upload commands are sequenced, reported, and explicitly cancelled or discarded. The cancellation case directly refines the higher-level discard behavior by identifying a concrete recognized command, D_MEM_DAT_CNCL, that causes an in-progress upload to be discarded. This provides a specific mechanism within observatory message handling that contributes to the broader requirement for discarding messages under defined conditions.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-CCM shall spawn tasks for DPU-CCM, DPU-DPA, DPU-DCX, DPU-SCUI, and DPU-TMALI at bootup.
lower_level_requirement: Control and Monitoringthe CCM Control Task initializes the DPU FSW. It is the responsibility of the CCM Control Task to establish a successful boot. It does so by blocking on temporary semaphores, each with a 5 second timeout, after spawning the SCU Interface Task and the CCM Command Task. If both of these tasks report a successful initialization by giving the semaphore, the CCM Control Task toggles the BC_INDEX parameter in EEPROM to indicate a successful boot. If either task does not report a successful initialization, the CCM Control Task disables the watchdog strobe to effect a reboot of the DPU. The rationale for selecting the successful initialization of these two tasks as the definition of a successful boot is that the DPU FSW requires these tasks, as a minimum, to establish ground contact and provide commandability.Once this initialization is complete, the task blocks on a binary semaphore which is given by the SCUI Command ISR upon arrival of the 1 Hz Clock Message. In the event a Clock Message does not arrive, the semaphore will time out after 1.5 seconds. The CCM Control Task remains alive to create and transmit DPU housekeeping at the appropriate intervals, perform various periodic processing tasks, and to process memory dump commands.The final call to ccmErrEnq() is performed in order that if an error occurs in an interrupt service routine, a global variable is set to the value of the errno which is then enqueued into the Error/Event Queue as part of this tasks normal processing.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement describes the CCM Control Task's boot-time behavior, including spawning the SCU Interface Task and the CCM Command Task and using their initialization status to determine successful DPU boot. This directly refines the higher-level requirement that DPU-CCM spawn specified DPU-related tasks at bootup by specifying concrete boot orchestration logic, initialization checks, and failure handling for spawned tasks.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-CCM shall spawn tasks for DPU-CCM, DPU-DPA, DPU-DCX, DPU-SCUI, and DPU-TMALI at bootup.
lower_level_requirement: InitializationThe TMALI CSC is initialized by spawning the tmaliTask() with the startup default parameters. This task will allocate memory for the TMALI_EVENT_QUEUE, install DCI ISRs, initialize static variables and data structures, and then enter an end-less loop in which it transfers the data from the DCI to the TMALI queue, throttled by the semaphore semDciWait.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement directly operationalizes part of the bootup task-spawning requirement by specifying that the TMALI CSC is initialized through spawning tmaliTask(). TMALI corresponds to one of the named components in the higher-level requirement, and the lower-level text details the startup behavior and initialization actions performed by that spawned task.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-CCM shall produce DPU_HK at a commandable rate, with a default of 10 seconds.
lower_level_requirement: Setting Frame Depth in DCIThe optimum frame depth will be determined with benchmark testing. The default frame depth is 10 frames. Given the above data, it will take approximately 24 msec to read 10 maximum-sized frames at the maximum data transfer rate.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement defines a configurable/default data acquisition parameter, the DCI frame depth, and quantifies the time required to read the default set of frames. This operational timing and buffering behavior directly supports the higher-level requirement to produce DPU_HK at a commandable rate by showing that the default frame handling can be completed well within the stated 10-second default production interval.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-CCM shall monitor the status of DPU-SCUI, DPU-CCM, DPU-DCX, DPU-TMALI, and DPU-DPA by examining their TASK_INFO and report this information in DPU_HK.
lower_level_requirement: Control and MonitoringThe DPU produces eight types of housekeeping packets.
label: trace
rationale: The higher-level requirement specifies that the DPU-CCM must monitor several DPU components and report their status information in DPU_HK housekeeping data. The lower-level requirement directly supports this by establishing that the DPU produces housekeeping packets, which are the reporting mechanism through which such monitored status information can be conveyed. Although it is more general and does not name the specific TASK_INFO sources, it operationalizes the required housekeeping output context.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-CCM shall maintain counts of both the number of commands successfully received and rejected and report the parameters in DPU_HK.
lower_level_requirement: Public FunctionsThis routine gets housekeeping data stored for the TMALI CSC including some DCI parameters and resets the tmali internal counters to zero. When the caller supplied pointer to a TMALI_HK structure is NIL no data is returned but the tmali internal counters are still reset to zero.Two of the four error counters are updated within an ISR context, this requires a task switch safe implementation of these counters. Within VxWorks this could be solved using a counting semaphore. In the TMALI CSC design a faster method was used by using a free running error counter and a careful update of the reported number of errors, using an extra temporary variable. As the increment and assignment of the 32 bit unsigned integers themselves are atomic operations the resulting counters are task safe and no error events are lost. This means that the sum of the errors reported by the tmaliHkGet() function is equal to the total numbers of errors that occurred, no error reports are lost due to the update of the internal structures.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement operationalizes reporting housekeeping data by defining a routine that returns TMALI housekeeping data, including DCI-related parameters, and resets internal counters after retrieval. Its description of task-safe error counter handling ensures that rejected/error events are accurately accumulated and reported without loss, directly supporting the higher-level need to maintain and report command reception/rejection counts in DPU_HK.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-TMALI shall provide a function which sets the current event bit ordering mode in the DCI driver.

Its TRUE/FALSE parameter behavior defines how the current event bit ordering mode is selected between special arrangement and default no-rearrangement modes, which is the function requested for the DCI driver.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-TMALI shall configure the DCI interface data timeout at startup as specified by TMALI_TIMEOUT provided during initialization. The default value shall be N milliseconds and shall be capable of being modified dynamically.
lower_level_requirement: Public FunctionsThis routine provides a means to get the current data timeout value used by the DCI. The returned value is the current timeout in milliseconds.The timeout is discussed in document 036911400, section 4.3.2.4.1.3.

rationale: The higher-level requirement concerns the DCI interface data timeout value, including its configured startup value, default, and dynamic modification capability. The lower-level requirement directly supports this by specifying a public routine that exposes the current DCI data timeout in milliseconds, enabling verification or use of the configured and dynamically changed timeout value. Thus it refines the observable access to the same timeout parameter governed by the higher-level requirement.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-TMALI shall utilize SCM_DCI_SR, along with ERRNO provided by DPU-DCI to decode errors and place them on an error queue for DPU-CCM.

If errno is set after the error queues are created, it is queued to the Error Queue by calling ccmErrEnq().

It also refines the behavior for the boot-time condition when the queue has not yet been created.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-TMALI shall utilize SCM_DCI_SR, along with ERRNO provided by DPU-DCI to decode errors and place them on an error queue for DPU-CCM.

This directly supports the higher-level requirement’s need to use ERRNO from DPU-DCI to decode and queue errors, because it defines how error information is made available for subsequent decoding and handling.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-TMALI shall place the starting address of the event ring buffer in TMALI_HK.

rationale: The higher-level requirement concerns making the event ring buffer available by placing its starting address in TMALI_HK. Thus, it directly supports the mechanism for processing events whose buffer address is established by the higher-level requirement.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-SCUI shall receive command messages in the form of Telecommand Packets from the SCU and make them available to the DPU-CCM.
lower_level_requirement: Command HandlingWhen a command arrives from the SCU (via the 1553 interface) or the ICU (via the SSI interface), the respective ISR will enqueue the command packet into a Command Queue, and then give the semaphore to awaken the ccmCmdTask(). Since it is possible for the DPU to send a command to itself, commands may arrive at interrupt context or task context. Therefore the CCM maintains two queues one for interrupt context which is not semaphore protected, and one for task context which is semaphore protected.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement operationalizes how command messages received from the SCU are handled inside the DPU: the ISR enqueues the command packet and signals ccmCmdTask for further processing. This directly supports making SCU-originated telecommand packets available to the DPU-CCM by defining the queuing and task-wakeup mechanism used to deliver them. Additional details about ICU input and separate queues do not break the trace because the SCU command path is explicitly covered.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-SCUI shall receive command messages in the form of Telecommand Packets from the SCU and make them available to the DPU-CCM.
lower_level_requirement: Receiving Commands from the SpacecraftThe DPU/SCU interface specifies that commands for the DPU will be transmitted from the SCU to the DPU on a separate MIL-STD-1553 subaddress. The SCU Interface Command Reader ISR, scuiCmdReadISR(). consists of an ISR installed on a specific MIL-STD-1553 subaddress corresponding to the command subaddress for the INSTRUMENT X DPU. This ISR is installed at initialization by scuiInit(). Upon interrupt, the scuiCmdReadISR() reads a single telecommand from the 1553 bus, checks the length and checksum, and then forwards valid commands to the Command and Control CSC for dispatch via ccmCmdEnq(). Errors are reported by incrementing an invalid command counter.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement directly operationalizes receiving telecommand packets from the SCU by specifying the MIL-STD-1553 command subaddress, interrupt handler, and validation steps used to read commands from the spacecraft interface. It also implements the required availability to the DPU-CCM by forwarding valid commands to the Command and Control CSC via ccmCmdEnq(). Thus, it provides a concrete mechanism for the higher-level DPU-SCUI command reception and handoff behavior.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-SCUI, in the event of a buffer full condition, shall discard new data, return an error to the caller, and report an error condition to the DPU-CCM.
lower_level_requirement: Error Collection and ReportingThe DPU-CCM CSC provides a centralized error reporting interface, ccmErrEnq(), that other FSW tasks use to report errors. Each time it wakes, ccmTask() checks to see if it is time to form an error/event packet for transmission to the ground. If so, ccmTask() calls ccmHkMkError() to actually create the packet and forward it to DPU-SCUI for transmission to the ground.
label: trace
rationale: The higher-level requirement requires DPU-SCUI to report an error condition to DPU-CCM when a buffer-full condition occurs. The lower-level requirement defines the DPU-CCM error reporting interface, ccmErrEnq(), used by other flight software tasks to report errors, which provides the mechanism by which such an error condition can be accepted and centrally handled. It also describes how DPU-CCM packages reported errors for later transmission, supporting the required error-reporting behavior.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-SCUI shall report errors to the DPU-CCM for inclusion in the DPU Housekeeping information.
lower_level_requirement: External Program InterfacesThis routine copies the BIT Results into bitHk for inclusion in the DPU Housekeeping.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement operationalizes how diagnostic error/status information is prepared for DPU Housekeeping by copying BIT Results into the bitHk housekeeping data structure. This directly supports the higher-level requirement’s objective of making DPU-SCUI error information available for inclusion in DPU Housekeeping, even though it specifies the internal routine/data handling rather than the reporting interface to DPU-CCM.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU compression software shall report errors to the DPU-CCM for inclusion in the DPU Housekeeping information.
lower_level_requirement: Public FunctionsThis routine is called by any CSC in order to report an error or event that should be included in DPU housekeeping. If this routine is called from interrupt context a static global variable, ccmISRError, is set so that the error can be enqueued later (see ccmCtrlTask()). This is done since the error/event queue is semaphore-protected and a semaphore cannot be taken in an ISR. The error queue semaphore has priority inversion set to reduce conflicts between multiple callers should a priority inversion situation arise. This routine also replaces frequently occuring errors with a special repeat error code. The repeat error code is a special error code that follows a normally reported error code to indicate that the normally reported error code previously reported has occurred more than once in the last high rate reporting period
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement defines a public routine used by CSCs to report errors or events for inclusion in DPU housekeeping, directly operationalizing the higher-level need to report errors to the DPU-CCM for housekeeping information. It further specifies implementation behavior for interrupt-context reporting, queuing, semaphore protection, and repeat-error handling, all of which support reliable delivery of reportable errors/events into the housekeeping mechanism.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-TIS shall provide the capability for an application program to set the value of the SC_TIME register(s) on the SCM and enable the 1PPS clock jam register, if automatic time synchronization is enabled.
lower_level_requirement: Structural DesignThe TIS CSC provides a library of functions to* initialize the DPU clock hardware at startup,* maintain synchronization of the DPU clock with the Spacecraft clock,* provide a function for use by other applications to retrieve the current values of the DPU clock and the UT Delta, and provide functions for use by the CCM command dispatcher to alter the configuration of the clock interface.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement describes the TIS component providing library functions that configure and maintain the DPU clock interface, including functions used by the command dispatcher to alter clock-interface configuration. This directly supports the higher-level capability for an application to set spacecraft time register values and enable clock-jam behavior when automatic synchronization is active, because those actions are part of controlling synchronization between the DPU clock and spacecraft clock hardware.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-TIS shall report errors to an application program by setting the ERRNO task variable and returning ERROR.
lower_level_requirement: Error Collection and ReportingAt boot time, no error queue exists because it has yet to be created. Errors that occur in this early stage of error reporting are assigned directly to the global task variable errno. The reader may refer to the VxWorks Programmers Guide, section 2.3.7 for more information on errno. If errno is set after the error queues are created, it is queued to the Error Queue by calling ccmErrEnq().
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement operationalizes how errors are reported through the errno task variable, including the boot-time case where errors are assigned directly to the global errno variable. This directly supports the higher-level requirement’s mandate to report errors to an application program by setting ERRNO; it further refines the behavior by distinguishing what happens before and after error queues are created.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-ICUI shall provide an API for other CSCs to transmit messages to the ICU.
lower_level_requirement: InitializationThe ICUI CSC is initialized by calling icuiInit(). The icuiInit() function opens the SSI interface port to the ICU, installs the transmit and receive ISRs, and enables Transmit Message Mode in the SSI Driver CSC. The icuiInit() function is called by the CCM Control Task at bootup.
label: trace
rationale: The higher-level requirement requires the DPU-ICUI to expose capability for other CSCs to send messages to the ICU. The lower-level requirement supports and operationalizes that capability by initializing the ICUI CSC, opening the SSI interface to the ICU, installing transmit/receive interrupt handlers, and enabling Transmit Message Mode in the SSI Driver CSC. These initialization steps are necessary to make the message-transmission API functional for other CSCs at runtime.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-ICUI shall report errors to DPU-CCM for inclusion in the DPU_HK.
lower_level_requirement: Control and MonitoringEvery time the CCM Control executes, it calls ccmPerProcess() to handle periodic processing responsibilities. Such responsibilities include analog to digital conversion updates, DPU task monitoring, ICU heartbeat message production, and watchdog strobe. The ccmHealthChk() function, called by ccmPerProcess() verifies the execution of other tasks by monitoring the amount of time that has elapsed since each task last reported. Other tasks report their execution to the CCM Control Task by calling the function, ccmTaskReport(), providing their task index. Each task has an expected execution frequency, and if a task does not execute as expected, an error is reported in DPU housekeeping. If the Command Dispatch Task fails to report for an extended period, the DPU will execute a reboot, since it is impossible to command the DPU if this task is not executing, otherwise it will strobe the watchdog
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement operationalizes error reporting for DPU housekeeping by describing how CCM periodic processing monitors task execution and reports an error in DPU housekeeping when a task fails to execute as expected. This directly supports the higher-level requirement’s objective of making errors available to DPU-CCM for inclusion in DPU_HK, specifically through CCM health checking and task report monitoring.

higher_level_requirement: The centroid confirmation engineering mode shall produce a PROD_CENTROID_CONF. This mode shall divide a full frame image into a certain regions. Each region shall be processed to form an 8x8 confirmation image. The certain confirmation images shall be sent to the solid state recorder as one data product.
lower_level_requirement: Centroiding Confirmation (CC) Engineering ModeThe purpose of Centroiding Confirmation Engineering Mode is to determine the validity of derived channel boundaries. Detector events are collected and histogrammed for a commanded integration time. The full field is divided into 8x8 sub-Instrument Ys, each of ExEcentroided (by 8) pixels. These sub-Instrument Ys are then modulo binned to produce a set of 8x8 pixels pseudo-Instrument Ys. The Instrument Ys are column (y axis) ordered, as are the pixels within them. These pseudo Instrument Ys are transmitted to the ground.
label: trace
